learning_objective: 🎯 Let us learn the golden rule of friendship between a Subject and its Verb!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Subject and the Verb are best friends. If the Subject is singular (just one), the verb must be singular. If the subject is plural (many), the verb must be plural!
A singular noun takes a singular verb. Singular verbs usually end with an 's'. Example: The dog (singular) barks (singular verb with s).
A plural noun takes a plural verb. Plural verbs do not have an 's' at the end. Example: The dogs (plural) bark (plural verb without s).
Even though 'I' and 'You' are singular, they are rule breakers! They act like plurals and take a plural verb. Example: 'I play' and 'You play' (not plays).

fun_activity.title: 🧩 The Matching Game
fun_activity.instructions: Write 'He', 'They', 'The Cat', and 'The Cats' on pieces of paper. Match them correctly with two other pieces that say 'jumps' and 'jump'!

quick_recap: ⭐ A singular subject needs a singular verb (usually ends in s).
⭐ A plural subject needs a plural verb (no s at the end).
⭐ The pronouns 'I' and 'You' are special exceptions and usually take a plural verb.
